raw_response:
Well, spring is here and it's time to get the cotton in the ground. I've been doing this for 10 years now on my 10.1 mu, and I've got a pretty good feel for what works in Quzhou.

Let me think through my season. I'm 38, finished middle school, and I've got a household of four. My wife and I handle most of the farm work, but our older kid is in school and my wife also does some off-farm work when she can, so labor is tight during the busy times. We can't be everywhere at once.

**Cotton — 10.1 mu, single cropping**

I'll plant in mid-to-late April, probably around April 20th. That's when folks around here usually get their cotton in. The soil is warming up by then. I'll aim to harvest from September through October, with multiple picks — cotton doesn't all mature at once.

For seed, I'll buy improved cotton seed from the local shop. I used to save my own seed but the yields weren't as good, and the improved varieties resist pests better. Costs me about 35 yuan per mu for seed.

Fertilizer — well, the extension guy last year said something about 12-15 kg of nitrogen per mu, but honestly I've been doing about 16 kg nitrogen per mu total and it works for me. I apply it in two goes: about 10 kg/mu as base fertilizer before planting, mixed into the soil, and then another 6 kg/mu at flowering stage in July when the plants really need it. I don't bother with phosphorus and potassium much — the soil here seems okay for those, and fertilizer is expensive. Every yuan counts with my household budget.

I'll irrigate probably twice this year. Once right after planting if the spring is dry, and once during peak flowering in July or August when the heat hits. Pumping water from the well costs money — electricity isn't cheap — so I won't overdo it. If we get decent rain I might cut it to once. I'm not one of those business farms that can afford to water whenever they feel like it.

Pesticides — yes, I'll spray. Cotton gets bollworms and aphids around here, and the weeds come up fast. I'll use herbicide before planting and maybe once more early on, plus insecticide 2-3 times during the season when I see pests. I watch the fields closely. I do the spraying myself with a backpack sprayer. Costs about 80 yuan per mu total for chemicals.

Tillage — I'll plow once with the small tiller I have, then level the field by hand. Nothing fancy. Between winter and spring I'll turn the soil over and break up the clods. Takes time but I don't have a big tractor, so that's how it goes.

Labor — I'll put in about 25 family days myself over the season, and I'll probably hire 8-10 days of labor, mostly for picking in the fall when the bolls open. My wife helps when she can but she's busy. Picking cotton is backbreaking work and there's a lot of it across 10 mu. Hired labor runs about 120 yuan per day around here.

Yield — I'm hoping for about 280 kg of lint per mu if the weather cooperates. Last year I got around 260, but the rain was a bit off. If I get good rain and manage the pests, 280 is realistic. I've seen neighbors get 300 but I don't count on it.

Total input costs — seed, fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation pumping, hired labor — I'm looking at around 1,650 yuan for the season. That's a big chunk of cash. I could spend more on fertilizer, but then what if the price drops? I'd rather have some cash in hand for emergencies. My neighbor across the way always puts on more fertilizer than me, but he also has more mu and his son working full-time on the farm. I do what I can afford.
